newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures narrowly mixed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures narrowly mixed in quiet trade.

text.p: U.S. debt futures were narrowly mixed in early quiet trading, with most contracts directionless amid tight ranges.

June Treasury bond futures were close to Wednesday's closing level and above 108-29/32, the equivalent of a seven-percent cash yield. Several traders said that cash levels would be key areas to watch for June T-bonds. The 7-1/8-percent cash yield equivalent is 107-3/32, according to Optima Technical Research.
"People are looking for direction right now," a Eurodollar trader said.
"It seems they're looking for something to tell them to sell them," he said.
He said debt futures could remained stymied -- with the risk to the downside -- until minutes from the March Federal Open Market Committee meeting are released later today.

Traders said the minutes could give a clue into the mindset of Fed policymakers. The Fed raised the fed funds target 25 basis points March 25 to 5.50 percent, but left policy unchanged at its May 20 meeting.
"We're just waiting for the minutes," the Euro trader said.
Traders said flows in T-bonds and Eurodollars were thin, with lethargy possible heading into the long holiday weekend.
"If we're busy at all tomorrow it'll be surprising," the trader said.
Bond futures close early Friday at 1210 CDT/1710 GMT and Eurodollars close early at 1200 CDT/1700 GMT. Trade will be shut on Monday to observe Memorial Day.
June T-bonds matched Wednesday's 109-03/32 two-week low early in the session, but that level held early minor losses.
Traders noted scant reaction to the latest weekly jobless claims.
Claims rose to 322,000 in the May 17 week from a revised 317,000 in the prior week.

At 0848 CDT/1348 GMT, June T-bonds were up 3/32 at 109-12/32, 10-year notes were up 1/32 at 107-6/32, muni bonds were up 8/32 at 116-14/32, Sept T-bills rose 0.010 to 94.560, and December Eurodollars fell 0.005 to 93.730.
